contract: aider unknown-model handling is explicit (no silent capability claims)

limitations: json5 not installed: used an in-process shim that parses strict JSON plus line comments (the subset used by aider metadata files).
oslex not installed: used a shlex-based shim (aider.utils only needs oslex.join for shell escaping, which this contract does not exercise).
litellm not installed: used an in-process stub reproducing litellm's unmapped-model behaviour for get_model_info/validate_environment.

results.expectation: register_litellm_models returns the loaded filename and stores each fixture entry exactly as declared (no capability keys injected).
An undeclared model resolves to an empty dict: absence is explicit, no cost/context/capability values are fabricated.
Prefix-stripping only applies when the declared entry's litellm_provider matches the prefix, so a bare name does not inherit another model's metadata.
sanity_check_model flags the unknown model (returns True) and emits the explicit 'Unknown ...' warnings instead of silently continuing.

warnings: Warning for meta/ghost-404: Unknown which environment variables are required.
Warning for meta/ghost-404: Unknown context window size and costs, using sane defaults.

results.expectation: Unknown models fall back to the documented 1024-token defaults and claim no optional settings (accepts_settings == []), so no unsupported capability is advertised.
A fixture entry with only context/provider/mode yields exactly those keys on lookup: missing capability and cost keys stay absent rather than defaulting to permissive values.
An explicit 'supports_function_calling: false' survives lookup as False (explicit denial), and metadata never silently enables settings such as thinking_tokens/reasoning_effort on the Model object.
